text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementNeuroscienceThe Teenage Girl Who Remembers EverythingA conversation with a scientist about a 16-year-old who has highly superior autobiographical memoryKFBy Kristen French1:00 PM CDT on October 27, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe memory is fallible. We misremember and forget the events of our lives all of the time. But a small number of individuals seem to have exceptional recall for the mundane details of their personal lives without even trying. Give them a date, and they can bring to mind the sandwich they ate for lunch, the sneakers they wore, the soft rain that fell in the afternoon.In 2006, the first clinical case of such a person was identified, and the condition was given a name: Highly Superior Autobiographical Memory, or HSAM. Some experts propose that there may be no more than 100 or so people on Earth with the condition.Read more: “Faulty Memory is a Feature not a Bug”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
